verdict: 2026-08-02 19:45:22 PDT — The edit locations are proportionate and add no dependency, but the design conflates a pre-code test plan with evidence that future assertions fail. Its own test notes also expose gaps in the proposed contract.

findings.title: A pre-code plan cannot prove future assertions are falsifiable
findings.locus: Problem; Design sketch — Step 5 and Step 6
findings.claim: The sketch adds a spec-time list of negative cases and a reviewer that judges whether they came from the criteria. Because no assertion exists at frame time and no later workflow step executes those regressions against the implemented tests, this cannot support the stated outcome that a dead assertion surfaces at the frame consult. A sound plan can still be implemented with an impossible regex or another assertion that never exercises its negative case. Calling the plan “falsification evidence” creates an assurance the workflow does not establish.
findings.alternative: Keep the criterion-derived plan at frame time, but distinguish it from evidence and require the implemented tests to be exercised against each planned negative case before the gate is accepted. If that execution remains deferred to the /review companion, narrow this story’s claim to test-design guidance rather than detection of dead assertions.
findings.win: Adds the missing point where negative cases are checked against real tests, allowing an unfalsifiable assertion to be detected; alternatively, narrowing the claim removes a false guarantee from the global workflow contract.

findings.title: The gate-red rule lacks an oracle model for manual criteria
findings.locus: Acceptance criteria 1–2; Test notes — AC5; Design sketch — Step 5
findings.claim: The proposed global rule requires a regression per AC that “must turn the gate red,” with N/A allowed only when the whole sketch is mechanical. This story immediately violates that contract for AC5: `git diff --name-only` only prints files and still exits successfully when an extra file appears, yet AC5 declares falsification N/A although the sketch is not mechanical. Documentation, review, and process criteria often have manual oracles, so universal automated-gate language invites pretend-red checks and silent passes.
findings.alternative: Require every AC to name a plausible regression and the oracle that detects it, with an explicit mode such as automated gate, manual inspection, or reviewer judgment and a reason when automation is unavailable. Reserve “turn the gate red” for executable checks; for AC5, either use an allow-list comparison that exits nonzero or label the scope check as manual rather than N/A.
findings.win: Eliminates the first loophole in the new contract, makes pass/fail semantics explicit, and lets one declarative template cover code, documentation, and process stories without fake automation.

findings.title: The story’s own falsification plan is assertion-shaped
findings.locus: Test notes — AC1 / AC2 / AC3 / AC4
findings.claim: The planned mutations are “red on main,” deleting the sentences that the new `has` checks pin, and editing their pinned phrases. Those cases are derived from the planned grep implementation—the anchoring failure the new reviewer sentence is supposed to reject—not from the semantic criteria. They do not separately challenge applying the rule to only some ACs, omitting the empty-result case, allowing an unexplained mechanical N/A, or permitting an implementation-derived reviewer plan.
findings.alternative: State negative cases from each criterion before referring to grep: one AC has no falsification entry; a presence/shape AC omits the wholly absent result; a mechanical story gives N/A without a reason; or the reviewer accepts a mutation described in terms of a selector/assertion rather than required behavior. Then choose stable `has` strings broad enough that each relevant semantic weakening breaks its drift check.
findings.win: Makes the first example comply with the policy it introduces and demonstrates that the two permitted drift assertions pin the required semantics rather than merely proving that their target strings can be deleted.
